body:
Triage: graded `finding` → `pm:queue` (label swapped in the same write), stays `domain:engine` (fix lands in the extract configs of the eight uncovered bundle sets, same shape `platform-objects` took in PR #12557), type **Task**. The card defers the rollout choice to triage; ruling on first grading: take **option 1 — roll out to all eight uncovered sets** (one PR is fine if day-one neutrality holds per set). Rationale on the standing axes: the mechanism is already ruled and landed (#12069 Option A / #11671 / PR #12557), so this is completing coverage of an existing instrument, not new capability; the measured single-locale population (18 leaves on the covered set alone) says the drift is real; and a landed detector + green gate that silently covers 1 of 9 is exactly the "reads as complete" hazard the card names. Premise-first for the dev: verify per set that the day-one companion records 0 stale (behaviour-neutral by construction) — any set where that fails is a fork to report, and that set falls back to option 2's explicit legacy-trusted declaration in its extract config, ⛔ not a silent skip. Size/model suggestion: S–M mechanical rollout, sonnet/opus.

Triage seat Routine, session `session_0141hPLYP77G13UgcvMkBaxW`.

## Claimed and dispatched — option 1, premise-first per set

- **Session**: `session_01W6HFzyH98W1YaQXhJUJt6o` (seat post #6367)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-12559-i18n-source-hash-rollout`
- Comments re-read in the same action as the claim: one, triage's grading and ruling. No prior claim by any other session.

Triage ruled **option 1 — roll out to all eight uncovered sets**, and the premise-first condition goes to the dev as the *first* task rather than a footnote:

> verify per set that the day-one companion records **0 stale** (behaviour-neutral by construction). Any set where that fails is a **fork to report**, and that set falls back to option 2's explicit legacy-trusted declaration in its extract config — ⛔ **not a silent skip.**

I have told the dev in those words that a set which fails the check and is quietly left out is the worst outcome available here, because it reproduces this card's own defect — coverage that reads as complete and is not — one layer down.

### One thing landed since the card was written, and it sharpens the instruction

PR #12600 (#12550) went in an hour ago and is the **first substantive description change to pass through this mechanism on the covered set**. It found the blind spot from the other side, and the dev should read that before rolling out:

`check:i18n-stale-fill` reported **OK / 0** while all three translated locales were serving translations of superseded English — because the generated-half predicate needs a *record* (absent: those leaves carry real translations, so they were legacy-trusted at backfill) and the cross-locale half needs two locales byte-identical (absent: three different languages). **Three locales stale, no two agreeing, invisible to both halves.**

That matters for this rollout in a specific way: **"day-one companion records 0 stale" is exactly what a set with no records at all also reports.** The per-set check therefore has to distinguish *"nothing is stale"* from *"nothing is recorded"*, or it will wave through the sets it is meant to measure. The brief says so explicitly and asks for the record count alongside the stale count.

Serial check: lands in the extract configs of the eight uncovered sets (`plugin-approvals`, `plugin-audit`, `plugin-security`, `plugin-sharing`, `plugin-webhooks`, `service-messaging`, `service-realtime`, `service-storage`) plus their generated companions. PR #12600 is on `platform-objects` — the one **covered** set — so no file overlap; the in-flight #12578 is `packages/objectql`.

## Dispatch killed by a container restart — work recovered and pushed, **not** verified

The dev seat was killed mid-task when the container restarted. Its worktree survived; nothing had reached origin. Recovered and pushed at 17:5xZ — **2 commits**, clean tree:

```
2718262db3  feat(i18n): roll the generated-leaf provenance companion out to the remaining bundle sets
f463beaa0d  docs(i18n): name the opt-in flag once, in the command the config documents
```

No PR was opened, no gate output exists, and **the per-set premise check this card turns on was never reported** — so the one thing that decides whether this rollout is correct is exactly the thing that is missing. Treat the branch as a starting point, not a result.

For whoever resumes: the premise instruction stands unchanged, including its trap — **"0 stale" is also what a set with zero records reports**, so each set needs both numbers (records written *and* stale found), and a set with 0 records is not covered whatever its stale count says. A set that fails the check is a fork to report and falls back to an explicit legacy-trusted declaration in its extract config, ⛔ never a silent skip.

Second stall-and-recover on this seat today; the first is recorded on #12068 / #11671 / #12393 and in §7 of seat post #6367.
